references.text: The original instruction to make the plate of pure gold with the inscription 'Holy to the Lord', as Exodus 39:30 describes its execution.
Describes how the plate was to be attached to the turban with a blue cord.
The continuation describing how the plate was attached to the turban with a blue cord, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
Moses places the holy crown on Aaron's turban during the consecration, referring to the gold plate.
The prophecy that 'Holy to the Lord' shall be written on the bells of the horses, extending the concept of holiness from the high priest's forehead band to the entire community.
Believers are to have God's name on their foreheads, as a parallel to the high priest's holy inscription—all of God's people are now priests.
Parallel use of the 'seal' metaphor to describe the inscription on both the stones of the breastpiece and the diadem.
